2606.19318.one_liner: S&P 500 returns summed over 20 to 120 days fit a tempered skew t, with the gain-side power law bending to a finite cutoff.

2608.01494.one_liner: Sizing an ETF portfolio by conformal interval width hit Sharpe 1.34 in development, then only 7 to 8.5 percent in the sealed lockbox.

2607.06502.one_liner: Across 200 published anomalies, the median long-short return outside microcaps after 2005 is 7 bp a month with a t-stat of 0.45.

2606.22796.one_liner: A Levy jump in Black-Scholes volatility yields closed-form ATM implied vol; fitted to VIX it mean-reverts with a 5.6 day half-life.

2511.16563.one_liner: Across 86 ETFs, normal-based 99 percent VaR is off by 20 percent on average; a weighted Student t is off by 3 percent.

2607.03082.one_liner: CVaR-optimized baskets of 30 active ETFs beat mean-variance on Sharpe, but 50 bp costs on 3,000 percent turnover erase most of the gain.

2601.06090.one_liner: The top eigenvalue of the Nordic stock correlation matrix jumps in 2008 and 2020, which the authors read as regime shifts.

2607.19311.one_liner: Adding tempered fractional memory to a GAS volatility model beats plain long memory on AMZN by 68 AIC points, in sample only.

2608.03925.one_liner: Fitting fractional Brownian motion on gamma activity time to a decade of S&P moments gives a Hurst near 0.45. No options tested.

2607.13112.one_liner: Ten components capture 91 percent of joint tail structure across 24 Fama-French portfolios and approximate portfolio VaR to within 1.25 percent.

2607.18624.one_liner: Long-only minimum variance weights flip discontinuously at correlation thresholds, so two nearly identical assets can swap the whole allocation. Structured shrinkage fixes it.

2512.21798.one_liner: TimeGAN and VAE synthetic S&P returns reproduce volatility and VaR within a few percent but give worse portfolio Sharpe than the real series.

2608.00127.one_liner: At Sharpe 1 over three years, expect a median max drawdown of 1.16 annual vols. Long memory multiplies that eightfold.

2607.20093.one_liner: Moving-average crossovers, RSI, MACD, Bollinger and sell-in-May all fail three pre-declared gates after 10 bp costs and multiple-testing control.

2607.09556.one_liner: A robust integer program picks a basket that never rebalances and still tracks the Dow with 0.40 percent out-of-sample error.

2512.24526.one_liner: Twelve LLMs picked and weighted stocks inside each S&P sector; the paper reports how those portfolios stack up against equal weight and max Sharpe.

2608.02917.one_liner: An automated market maker with a 3 to 4 percent fee band tracks a portfolio mandate more tightly than the incumbent index funds.

2606.26731.one_liner: Rolling rank correlation between VIX and SPY illiquidity peaks near 0.37 in stressed windows, setting the stress level for a hedging valuation adjustment.

2606.14798.one_liner: The knob between hierarchical risk parity and minimum variance is the same object as damping in spatial statistics, and it has a closed-form optimum.

2607.06117.one_liner: A gated QQQ versus DIA rotation earns 18.3 percent at Sharpe 0.94 after costs, beating QQQ on Sharpe but not on return.

2606.09025.one_liner: Two cash overlays on a fixed ten-ETF sleeve cut max drawdown from 34 to 18 percent and raised CAGR from 16.6 to 18.8 percent.

2512.12815.one_liner: After the January 2024 spot ETF approval, Bitcoin's link to the dollar and gold broke structurally while its link to the S&P did not.

2512.22109.one_liner: A sparse S&P tracker that mostly holds still runs 5 percent turnover over six years against 500 percent for rivals, costing 3 bp.

2606.16840.one_liner: Across 13 major coins the crash-side dependence graph stays near-complete over five years while the rally-side thins out, so crypto diversification only fails downward.

2607.03858.one_liner: US equity panels split into a persistent factor near Hurst 0.55 and an antipersistent one near 0.22, with the market mode turning cascade-like.

2512.23640.one_liner: Fitting gains and losses in the S&P with separate volatility parameters gives a skew t that captures the asymmetry a symmetric fit misses.

2606.31251.one_liner: Across 146 walk-forward folds, an SVM timing rule beats buy-and-hold only in the worst volatility regimes and loses badly in the best ones.

2512.02029.one_liner: Across 378 coins and 480 million simulated holds, the median two-year crypto position loses 28 percent net of fees while Bitcoin-only medians stay positive.

2607.19825.one_liner: Shrinking a rank-based covariance nonlinearly cuts minimum-variance portfolio volatility from 11.0 to 9.5 percent and turnover by 40 percent, at the same Sharpe.

2512.02166.one_liner: Splitting volatility memory into regime, fractional and clock gates shows fractional memory wins in EURUSD while regime and clock gates win in SPY.

2606.04153.one_liner: Forecasting the sign of monthly S&P returns conditional on their size turns $100 into $182 by 2021 after costs, versus $105 for buy-and-hold.

2512.02352.one_liner: A rank-invariant roughness estimator built from visibility graphs puts the VIX far from independent noise and implies a Hurst near 0.09.

2512.19986.one_liner: A covariance-aware projection lifts in-sample Sharpe 26% on 100 S&P names, but loses to the plain Euclidean version in two of three walk-forward years.

2512.18918.one_liner: Ten years of SEC Form 4 filings build an insider trading network whose coordinated clusters look nothing like shuffled or simulated nulls.

2512.05661.one_liner: Across 7,286 rolling 10-day VaR forecasts, Bayesian networks breach on exactly the same three days as plain historical simulation.

2606.23492.one_liner: Hidden Markov models with fat-tailed emissions pass distribution tests on SPY but fail out-of-sample on 11 of 30 individual stocks.

2512.20460.one_liner: Welch-Goyal predictors only forecast the equity premium when the yield curve was flat or inverted recently; out-of-sample R-squared rises from 2.6% to 4.1%.

2606.22615.one_liner: Fitting stochastic volatility in mean models by hidden Markov approximation runs about ten times faster than MCMC on four equity indices.

2606.26625.one_liner: Rolling mean-variance and CVaR portfolios of 30 commodity ETFs beat equal weight on Sharpe and cut tail loss, with no trading costs charged.

2512.06550.one_liner: Two Japanese bank mergers produced cumulative abnormal returns of 30% and 6%, though the estimate swings by half depending on the market model.

2606.08569.one_liner: Ranking stocks by a put premium implied from their own price tree earns 3.7% yearly on the S&P 500, far under buy and hold.

2606.31475.one_liner: An eigenvalue indicator from rogue wave physics flagged the 2008 VIX spike 18 trading days early, at 63% to 84% precision across three indices.

2512.17225.one_liner: A quantum field theory fit to S&P 500 returns reproduces crisis kurtosis the Ising model misses and beats rolling regression on next-day AAPL error.

2607.21826.one_liner: Log-periodic power law fits to Bitcoin and Ether place the 2017-2018 crash dates roughly right, fitted after the fact on a single window.

2608.04987.one_liner: Swapping the covariance matrix for a multifractal fluctuation matrix gives the lowest drawdown and expected shortfall across four assets, reported only as figure bands.

2606.22719.one_liner: A leakage-controlled LLM ranks equity style factors with rank IC 0.13, not statistically significant, and the traded version loses money after costs.

2606.27932.one_liner: A standard self-similarity test rejects 47% of the time instead of 1%; a fractional-derivative version fixes it and puts stock indices near H=0.5.

2607.10297.one_liner: Portfolios of the 40 most peripheral stocks in a noise-filtered correlation network earned Sharpe 0.81 against 0.51 for the market, 2010 to 2022.

2607.03888.one_liner: An optimal local bandwidth for local Gaussian correlation buys little: adaptive tail estimates match the global ones within 0.01 on SPY, TLT and EEM.

2512.21791.one_liner: Scoring three synthetic return generators on fidelity, temporal structure and downstream use puts TimeGAN ahead of a VAE and ARIMA-GARCH on every axis.

2607.06908.one_liner: A participation-ratio rule finds a median of seven global factors in daily S&P 500 returns where the standard Onatski test usually finds one.

2512.10606.one_liner: Concentrating an equal-weight book in stocks whose signed-correlation balance deviates most from the market beat 1/N on four indices at hand-picked thresholds.

2511.21221.one_liner: Weighting other markets by forward validation raises Sharpe for dual-listed A and H share pairs and six US sector baskets, tested on 63 days.

2607.27461.one_liner: Three price-only matrices drive a long-short book at Sharpe 1.06 against the market's 0.78, then 1.32 against 1.14 in a live forward test.

2606.11962.one_liner: A composite-likelihood Hurst estimator puts log-VIX at 0.42 and beats method of moments on forecast error, by under a tenth of a percent.

2607.26188.one_liner: Bitcoin topped 525, 546 and 534 days after the last three halvings while Pi Cycle, Mayer, MVRV and Puell extremes decayed every cycle.

2512.01408.one_liner: Putting one Wasserstein ball on the drift prior instead of at every date raises Sharpe from about 0.35 to 0.48 on random 20-stock draws.

2607.19279.one_liner: Gaussian boson sampling clusters for statistical arbitrage reach Sharpe 2.25, statistically indistinguishable from ordinary spectral clustering at 2.04.

2512.12334.one_liner: Across 7,286 expected shortfall forecasts, EGARCH wins and Bayesian networks tie historical simulation, but every model fails the conditional backtest.

2512.23596.one_liner: Choosing training window length and model class by tournament raises out-of-sample R-squared on 17 industry portfolios to 4.9%, double a short fixed window.

2607.25189.one_liner: A two-dimensional Markov chain gives GARCH long memory with three parameters, still fitting 13 to 25 log-likelihood points worse than FIGARCH.

2607.01377.one_liner: Signed order flow built from daily volume predicts next-month stock returns; the two Kyle lambda estimators explain almost nothing and flip sign.

2606.31387.one_liner: Writing execution speed as a signature functional turns path-dependent statistical arbitrage into a concave quadratic program, tested on one pair for two months.

2512.19251.one_liner: In a panel of 18 coins, institutionally backed ones absorb about a third less market-wide volatility, with the backing label assigned by hand.

2512.23021.one_liner: A new PSD covariance estimator lifts a 10-asset tangency portfolio's out-of-sample Sharpe to 0.56 versus 0.51 for Gerber and shrinkage rivals.

2512.21823.one_liner: Restricted Boltzmann free energy failed to flag the COVID crash on a 19-series cross-asset panel; only the Gaussian variant tracked VIX spikes.

2512.12250.one_liner: A stochastic-volatility feed into an LSTM cut 21-day S&P 500 volatility forecast error to 5.3% MAPE, but the trading version only reached Sharpe 0.54.

2512.15113.one_liner: A genetic-algorithm-tuned SVR cut one-year-ahead price forecast error on five global indices by 20% versus LSTM, with no trading test.

2606.09104.one_liner: Stacking a Bayesian VAR ensemble, Student-t Black-Litterman and a TD3 agent on 29 Dow stocks returned 57% with Sharpe 1.72 over one test window.

2512.09224.one_liner: An exploratory mean-variance policy under jump diffusion beat the plain calibrated policy on Sharpe in 12 of 14 rolling S&P 500 test years.

2606.08283.one_liner: Hawkish and dovish LLM macro agents beat a deterministic z-score rule on commodity ETFs by 0.04 Sharpe, and survived costs the rule did not.

2511.17963.one_liner: An LSTM plus PPO allocator across stocks and crypto reached Sharpe 0.96, but plain PPO without the LSTM scored higher at 1.02.

2512.07860.one_liner: An LSTM ensembled with Levy jump-diffusion volatility paths hit R-squared 0.997 forecasting Brent and European index price levels.

2512.15739.one_liner: A Bayesian dynamic linear model beat GARCH-t on S&P 500 VaR coverage but still failed the conditional coverage test; the LSTM passed.

2606.26815.one_liner: Neural forecasts of the US and euro zero curve hit 56% and 53% directional accuracy, and the duration-managed bond strategy reached Sharpe 1.2.

2511.21873.one_liner: A graph attention network forecasting 79 FTSE 100 stocks did best with a 5-day window, and correlation graphs beat fundamental-ratio graphs.

2512.12924.one_liner: Five classic microstructure signal families tested over 34 out-of-sample quarters returned 0.55% a year against SPY's 13.2%, with t-statistic 0.96.

2606.30037.one_liner: Swapping a point head for a Gaussian mixture head lifted forecast skill more than changing the backbone; classical models still win at short horizons.

2606.27670.one_liner: A correlation graph attention model on 66 coins reached Sharpe 3.1 after costs, and time-mixing modules that help stocks hurt crypto.

2512.04099.one_liner: The transformer with the lowest crypto forecast error was not the most profitable; on Ethereum every model finished near zero return.

2607.12248.one_liner: The 80% directional accuracy claimed for fine-tuned foundation models is just the rising-market base rate; excess accuracy is negative.

2606.27100.one_liner: Six pretrained time-series foundation models took 8 of 10 return-forecast wins over trained baselines, but none beat a zero-return random walk significantly.

2606.15701.one_liner: A shifted data augmentation scheme cut Transformer index-level forecast error by two thirds and shrank the spread across ten random seeds.

2606.05733.one_liner: A streaming neural Hawkes graph over July 2022 news picked next-day extreme movers at 1.5 to 1.8 times the random rate.

2512.07867.one_liner: LLM-written macro stress scenarios produced VaR and CVaR roughly 3.7 times the historical bootstrap level for a 60/30/10 ETF portfolio.

2607.09820.one_liner: A network that learns a state-dependent Wasserstein radius returned 26% a year with Sharpe 1.30 on 20 S&P 500 names over one test window.

2607.15195.one_liner: A physics-informed offline RL policy trading under quadratic impact reached Sharpe 1.49 against 1.07 for equal weight, using a synthetic alpha.

2607.23068.one_liner: A compact neural minimum-variance model held Sharpe 1.12 at 3x leverage against 0.88 for hierarchical risk parity, and pushed the liquidation threshold higher.

2606.15473.one_liner: Turning daily LLM regime probabilities into a Belief-at-Risk measure produced spikes at the 2025 tariff shock, roughly ten times the calm baseline.

2512.02036.one_liner: Feeding 482 LSTM outputs into a random forest raised test AUC from 0.563 to 0.566, a gain well inside the confidence interval.

2512.16251.one_liner: Forcing a deep asset pricing model to reproduce nine analyst-consensus variables raised out-of-sample R-squared from 7.6% to 10.5% and long-short Sharpe to 1.44.

2608.04832.one_liner: Randomizing volatility so filtering ambiguity stays stationary improved deep hedging risk on 6 of 10 synthetic payoffs versus a standard learned benchmark.

2606.17383.one_liner: An LLM regime filter feeding Black-Litterman scored Sharpe 1.68, yet equal weight earned more, and the model's crisis probabilities were badly miscalibrated.

2512.01123.one_liner: A backtested options wheel on leveraged ETFs reports 15.3% a year with zero assignments across 1,563 puts, including 2008 and 2022.

2607.00475.one_liner: Across sixteen futures, equal weighting matched an LSTM allocator at zero cost and buried it at 10 basis points; only the transformer held up.
